Saga trial-specific follow-up: methods and uncertainty

## Separate results for the two Chicago trials

Appendix Table 5 reports eleventh-grade mathematics and high-school graduation outcomes separately for Study 1 and Study 2. The main article explicitly points to these cohort-specific results in footnote 17 on printed page 752. These are follow-up analyses of the existing trials, not additional experiments. ITT and TOT describe alternate estimands for the same outcome; neither they nor the pooled results add independent studies.

## Follow-up definition

The main article describes its pooled eleventh-grade outcomes using the year a student would have reached eleventh grade without retention. The appendix notes that students may have multiple eleventh-grade years. These records retain the appendix's reported eleventh-grade label; the handling of repeated grade years is not fully specified here, so a common elapsed follow-up interval is not assigned. Graduated ever refers to the observed window, whose terminal date has not been established, not lifetime graduation.

## Uncertainty and sample

Each estimate retains the reported standard error and outcome-specific number of observations. The appendix retains both randomizations for 65 Study 2 students randomized twice and clusters robust standard errors by individual. The control-complier mean is an estimate; the row's FDR q-value is not an ordinary per-estimand p-value. Low adjusted q-values for Study 1 math and higher q-values for Study 2 do not by themselves establish a between-study difference. Graduation point estimates are imprecise and do not establish either a benefit or no effect.
